channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Coforge launches CXNova, an agentic platform that hands the whole customer journey to AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Indian IT services firm Coforge launched CXNova on September 30 — an AI-native customer experience platform built on a multi-agent architecture, with content, context, and canvas agents orchestrated through a centralized control plane. The market noticed: shares traded about 4% higher in Mumbai.

item.title: RUMOR: did xAI buy dot.com to troll OpenAI's Dots launch? The redirect is real — the rest is unverified
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Reddit thread claims Elon Musk's xAI bought the domain dot.com and pointed it at Grok Bot around OpenAI's Dots launch. We checked the redirect ourselves: it's live. The buyer, the price, and the timing are all unverified.

item.title: Route every AI coding agent to any model from one menu bar: hands-on with magpie
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: magpie (yetone/magpie, MIT, 3,100+ stars in its first week) puts every AI agent's model in one menu-bar screen — click a value, pick a model. We installed it, routed Codex to DeepSeek and Claude Code to Kimi, and tested its local translation gateway. Every command verified.

item.title: Kodiact launches an AI-native simulation platform for direct materials: see the shock before it hits the P&L
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Kodiact's AI-native platform connects every material to its underlying price drivers and simulates multi-variable shocks across materials, suppliers, demand and energy — aimed at procurement teams still running category management on Excel.

item.title: One-shot a playable browser game with a frontier model: the workflow behind the Opus 5.5 demos
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A Reddit poster claims Sonnet 5.5 one-shot a 3D zombie FPS in 49 minutes — but the demos skip the workflow that makes it repeatable. Here’s the complete process: spec-first prompting, the debug loop, playtesting, juice, and shipping, with every step verified on a real game we built and ran.

item.title: Sepia: strip the AI out of your writing at the structural layer — hands-on with the 2.9K-star writing skill
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: Sepia is an MIT-licensed writing skill that de-AIs prose at the structural layer, not the word layer — 2,900+ GitHub stars in its first month. We installed it twice, validated its persona checker, ran its 94-test suite, and walked a release note through its full review protocol. Every command verified.

item.title: AI gave my brother independence: head-movement games built with Google Astra and Claude Opus 5.5
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: On r/singularity, a first-person post shows what the new wave of AI-built games looks like up close: three head-movement-controlled games, made with Google Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, for a brother with Tubb4a-related Leukodystrophy — released free and open source.

item.title: Page Agent: give any web page its own AI agent — hands-on with Alibaba's in-page GUI agent
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: Page Agent is Alibaba's MIT-licensed in-page GUI agent — 29,276 GitHub stars — that turns any website into a natural-language-operated page with one line of JavaScript. We installed page-agent@1.12.4, drove its real agent loop with a scripted model backend, and watched it fill forms, pick dropdown options, and click buttons. Every command verified.

item.title: DeepSeek gears up for a Shanghai IPO: CITIC begins due diligence, first CFO hired
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: China's most secretive AI lab is taking its first formal steps toward the public markets: a CITIC Securities team has begun IPO due diligence on site, DeepSeek has hired its first chief financial officer, and reports point to a $7.45 billion raise at a valuation of roughly $75 billion.

item.title: At IROS 2026, a year-old startup says robot intelligence is a hardware problem — meet LumiBot’s 10-micron fingers
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: LumiBot (Shiyue Technology), founded in 2025, took its dexterous hands, visuo-tactile sensors, and the Lumi-Mind manipulation model to IROS 2026 — arguing the embodied-AI data bottleneck is really a hardware problem.

item.title: Turn your AI agent into a research scientist: a hands-on tutorial for Scientific Agent Skills
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Scientific Agent Skills is a 168-skill, MIT-licensed library — roughly 47,000 GitHub stars — that teaches coding agents to do real science. We installed it, validated all 168 skill manifests, and ran one skill’s bundled tooling to produce a genuine figure. Every command verified.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO prospectus reveals $518B in compute commitments — most of it non-cancelable
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reuters reports Anthropic's confidential IPO prospectus locks the AI lab into at least $518 billion of cloud and infrastructure commitments over a decade — roughly 80% of it owed regardless of usage — as the Claude maker gears up for a listing that could top $2 trillion.

item.title: Nvidia wants insurers to underwrite the AI buildout: early talks would cover lenders if chip-backed loans go bad
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Financial Times reports Nvidia is in early talks with insurers to cover lenders to neoclouds if borrowers default and pledged chips can't be resold for enough — the third step in a seven-week push to turn AI hardware into an investable asset class.

item.title: Bain says AI needs $6 trillion a year by 2031 to pay for its data centers — $4.2T of it from markets that barely exist
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bain's annual tech report, out Tuesday, says AI must generate $6T in annual revenue by 2031 to justify the data-center buildout — but today's apps can only cover $1.8T. The other $4.2T must come from autonomous machines, physical AI, and brand-new markets like drug discovery and mental health.

item.title: Trump signs AI 'self-policing' accord with tech CEOs: voluntary reviews, a 10-person oversight board, and no new laws
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Trump and the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google, Nvidia and more signed a one-page accord at the White House: robust internal controls, independent audits, and board committees — all voluntary. Here’s what it actually requires, and what it leaves out.

item.title: Stop guessing which LLM fits your machine: a hands-on guide to llmfit
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: llmfit scans your CPU, RAM, GPU, and VRAM, then scores hundreds of open models on fit, speed, quality, and context — so you download the model that actually runs well. Install, recommend, simulate, and verify — every command verified against the project's README.

item.title: OpenAI in talks to raise $30B at a $1.4 trillion valuation — a bridge round before the IPO
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bloomberg reports OpenAI is in early-stage talks to raise at least $30B at a $1.4T valuation — a bridge round ahead of next year's IPO, surfacing one day after the Astra pullback.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra coding power at a fifth of the price
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI's DevDay keynote brought GPT-6.1 Sol, an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol that nearly matches flagship GPT-6 Astra on agentic coding, computer use, and professional work — at one-fifth of Astra's token price.

item.title: Stop writing your own agent loop: a hands-on tutorial for OpenAI's Agents API
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI’s DevDay put a managed agent harness behind a single API call. Build a long-running, tool-using agent on the Agents API — sessions, sandboxes, MCP tools, subagents, and cleanup — with every line verified against the official docs.

item.title: OpenAI’s DevDay got an AI-made Sam Altman × Dario Amodei parody — and Reddit identified the tool behind it
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: On OpenAI’s DevDay, the most-shared post on r/OpenAI wasn’t an announcement — it was a joke: an AI-generated music-video parody starring Sam Altman and Dario Amodei. The comments did what they do best, and named the tool that made it.

item.title: Impeccable: teach your AI coding agent to design like a design director — hands-on with the 72K-star skill
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: Impeccable, Paul Bakaus’s 72K-star design skill for AI coding agents, pairs 24 named design commands with 61 deterministic detector rules that run with no LLM and no API key. I scanned a deliberate AI-slop page hands-on — 12 findings down to zero — and documented every command.

item.title: Hands-on with NVIDIA Model Optimizer: quantize once, export anywhere
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: NVIDIA's Model Optimizer gained ~900 GitHub stars in four days: one Python API for quantization, pruning, distillation, and speculative decoding, plus a unified export to TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang. I ran INT8 weight-only quantization end-to-end on a CPU-only VM — 6.5 seconds, no quality loss, one-third smaller checkpoint — and documented the INT4 AWQ attempt the sandbox OOM-killed.

item.title: Flatkey raises $10M for one API key that reaches 100+ models and 1,000 tools — most of them below list price
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: San Jose's Flatkey announced a $10M Series A Tuesday after passing 10,000 developers in two months, pitching one key, one balance, and one invoice for 100+ official models and 1,000+ AI tools — at 60 to 90% of the labs' list prices.

item.title: Reco raises $55M to secure the AI agents your company doesn't know it has — AT&T Ventures leads
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AI security startup Reco announced Tuesday it has raised $55 million in additional strategic funding led by AT&T Ventures, bringing its total raised to $140 million. The company maps every AI agent operating inside a customer’s business — including the ones nobody authorized.

item.title: Cribl launches StreamAI: an AI gateway with a model router that cuts the token bill — free inference when the router picks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cribl's new StreamAI gateway routes each prompt to the cheapest model that gets the job done — and inference is free when the router picks the model. Its SecIT Bench found just a 17% accuracy spread but a 20x cost spread across 20 AI models.
